Off the Books: Storage Upgrades 1.5.0

WHAT IT DOES
You enlarge containers you own by dropping upgrade material on them: Metal Ingots on
bays and machines, an empty crate on another crate of the same kind, an empty Red Imp
Beer Case on another Red Imp Beer Case. A container never gets smaller. The mod needs
no other mod.

HOW TO USE IT
Drop the material on a closed container. The tooltip shows its size and the next step.
- Bays: drop a Metal Ingot on a Smuggler's Bay, Machine Bay, Storage Bay, Gunsmith
  Storage Bay or Chemist Storage Bay. Each ingot adds one column or one row, up to a limit per bay
  (for example Smuggler's Bay (Modified) 16x16, Storage Bay (Extended) 20x20).
- Loot crates: drop an empty, unlocked crate on another crate of the same kind. The
  crate you drop on grows and keeps its look; the other is used up. A crate can grow
  to six times its size: 7x5 becomes 19x11. Two enlarged crates can be joined. Every
  crate of the game and every 8x8 crate ends at 19x11 (an 8x8 crate takes three
  crates, not six). Crates of other base shapes can end on a different size.
- Red Imp Beer Case: drop an empty Red Imp Beer Case on another. It grows to three
  wide first (24x4), and the second row (24x8) comes with the sixth case. An enlarged
  case shows how full it is with the game's own pictures.
- Fridge, Wine Rack, Aquaculture and Rat Cage grow further with Metal Ingots once
  their own upgrades in the game are complete (Fridge 9x13 and 7x13, Wine Rack 12x8,
  Aquaculture and Rat Cage 24x16). The Water Tank's capacity grows from 12 to 48 in
  six steps.
With a mod that stacks the materials, a stack dropped on a bay, a crate or a machine
takes every step it covers, one after the other, and the rest of the stack stays where
it was. Switch this off with "A dropped stack upgrades as far as it reaches" to get one
step per drop.
When you trade an enlarged Smuggler's Bay to the janitor for a Smuggler's Bay
(Modified), the new bay keeps the gained columns and rows, within its limits and your
settings. What you left inside the old bay goes with it, as in the game.
Do not run this mod next to another mod that enlarges the same containers with the
same material: both would answer the same drop.

SETTINGS
All settings are in the Mods list and in Options, under Off the Books: Storage
Upgrades.
- A dropped stack upgrades as far as it reaches: one step per drop when off.
- Storage upgrades: allows new storage upgrades. Saved sizes are restored when it is off.
- Machine storage upgrades: allows Metal Ingots to enlarge machine storage.
- Drop an empty crate on another of the same kind to enlarge it: switches the crate
  upgrade.
- Red Imp Beer Case upgrades: switches the Red Imp Beer Case upgrade.
- How many crates one crate can grow to: 1 to 6, for crates and Red Imp Beer Cases.
  Lowering it does not shrink existing containers.
- One pair of settings per bay, "<bay name>: maximum columns" and "<bay name>: maximum
  rows": the largest size for new steps. You can lower them, not raise them.
- Smuggler's Bays take Machine Bays (off by default): lets an owned Machine Bay, with
  what is in it, go into an owned Smuggler's Bay at once. The game does not allow this.
- Storage Bays take Machine Bays (off by default): the same for an owned Makeshift
  Storage Bay, Storage Bay or Storage Bay (Extended).
Both Machine Bay settings need "Storage upgrades" on.

WHAT IT CHANGES IN A SAVE
Sizes are stored on the containers in your save. A crate remembers the size it started
with.

BEFORE YOU REMOVE THIS MOD
Without the mod the grids return to their usual size, and items in the extra space can
be lost on load. So empty enlarged containers first. In the shop, open Options, find
Off the Books: Storage Upgrades, switch on "Before removing this mod: list what to
move" and press Apply. The switch reads as off when Options is reopened. The window
lists containers with items wholly or partly outside the game's own grids, where they
are and how many items to move (a stack counts as one). It moves nothing. Move the
items and ask again. Inspect and empty any container marked "cannot tell" yourself.
Water capacity is not a grid: an upgraded Water Tank is marked "cannot tell". Lower its
contents to 12 million units first.

WHEN SOMETHING SEEMS WRONG
Player.log shows a line starting with [Storage Upgrades] when the mod meets a fault.

TRANSLATIONS
Translations are very welcome: every text is in Localization/en.csv. Send a translated
copy on GitHub: https://github.com/rnk-gaming/probably-stolen-mods/issues
